item.text:
Fork A: A1 — for: Keep JSON block-tree as the canonical non-developer surface because it is schema-validatable data, editor-friendly, diffable, and easier for AI to generate without inventing control flow. The key is that JSON does not become a second renderer: it compiles into the same internal render IR as Liquid, with the same components, permissions, and validation. — against: The risk is real: a proprietary layout DSL can accrete conditionals, responsive rules, animation knobs, query semantics, and eventually become a worse templating language that only you maintain. Liquid also has an existing mental model and ecosystem, while JSON layout errors can be harder for humans to repair. — what would move me: I would move to A2 if user testing showed non-developers and AI agents produce better, more maintainable Liquid than JSON, or if the JSON schema starts needing arbitrary expressions, loops, data queries, or CSS-like escape hatches to satisfy normal themes.

Fork B: B2 — for: Themes should not ship arbitrary client JS because same-origin browser execution can still exfiltrate data, deface pages, phish users, tamper with analytics, or become a supply-chain incident. Premium motion should come from signed, permission-scoped components/plugins referenced by id and configured by data, which preserves visual richness without making every theme install a code execution decision. — against: This reduces theme author freedom and slows premium visual work, especially for bespoke GSAP/Framer effects where a reviewed component catalog may lag market taste. It also creates platform burden: you must maintain enough motion primitives and a plugin review/signing pipeline good enough that designers do not fight the system. — what would move me: I would move toward B1 only with hard isolation, such as separate-origin or iframe execution with constrained postMessage APIs, no access to tenant/session/customer data, strong CSP, package signing, revocation, and clear user consent for code-capable installs.

Overall recommendation has not changed since Round 1: layered tiers still give the best split between safe marketplace authoring, AI-friendly composition, and a trusted developer escape hatch.

<<SWARM_END>>
